scores.claim_text: No single customer >= 10% of total net sales FY23-FY25
scores.M_check: Internal 10-K narrative (Mode A) + usaspending top-recipient identification (Mode B)
scores.M_value: USAspending top recipients show no single federal end-customer concentration; largest single DoD obligation is $1.04M (Strategic Buffer Bearing Steel) — far below any 10% threshold of $2,877M revenue (would require $287M from a single customer). Commercial customers (Boeing, engine OEMs) not visible in usaspending but mill supplier dependency on any single prime is a known structural risk; 10-K's no-concentration disclosure is internally consistent across three years.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 7 applies inversely: company declares NO concentration, so there is no 'unnamed Customer A' to identify. PASS.

scores.claim_text: $400M share buyback authorized July 2024; $101.9M executed by 6/30/2025; 100,000 shares Q4 FY25 at $240.72 avg
scores.M_check: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form 8-K (Mode A) + insider_vs_calendar.query_insider_sales_near_budget_events(cik='0000017843', window_days=14, start_date='2024-01-01', end_date='2026-05-20') (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: 50+ 8-K filings on record including capital-return cadence. Mode B: 46 Form 4 filings; 56 total insider sales worth $76.5M aggregate; 10 proximate to budget/fiscal events; 9 are DISCRETIONARY (non-10b5-1). signal=CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY. Most striking: 9 discretionary sales clustered 7 days AFTER the 2026-04-28 FY27 J-Book release totaling $5.53M, primarily by AKINS MARSHALL D (Chief Commercial Officer, ~$4.5M alone on 2026-05-05) and HART ANASTASIOS JOHN. Window: 14 days, kwargs exactly as specified.
scores.interpretation: Per prompt's explicit Mode B rule: 'If the call returns CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY signal: that is the highest-signal flag → SEVE or RED.' The Chief Commercial Officer (closest insider to A&D / federal-program sales pipeline) executed multi-tranche discretionary sales totaling >$4.5M within 7 days of the J-Book release, in addition to the buyback overhang absorbing dilution from compensation. This is a Mode B finding that the Mode A buyback-confirmation alone would have missed. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY — the capital-return narrative is being used as a price-support backstop while top commercial insider exits.

scores.claim_text: Material exposure to Boeing as commercial aviation customer (risk-factor disclosure naming Boeing as a 'key participant')
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Carpenter Technology') (Mode A) + edgar_fts(cik='0000012927') Boeing's filings (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Boeing (CIK 0000012927) shows 0 mentions of 'Carpenter Technology' in EDGAR full-text search. Carpenter's own 10-K mentions Boeing only once, embedded inside a forward-looking-statement risk factor, not as a named material customer.
scores.interpretation: Per heuristic 7: 0 mentions in counterparty's 10-K is SEVE only when (a) counterparty large [YES], (b) claim is material [Carpenter's claim is vague — Boeing is cited as risk, not as a >10% customer (Carpenter declares no 10% customer)], (c) revenue exceeds sub-tier disclosure thresholds [unknown]. Carpenter's Boeing reference is hedge-language not a revenue claim. The asymmetric absence (Carpenter discloses Boeing as risk; Boeing never names Carpenter as supplier) is MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY — flags Boeing-dependency narrative inconsistency without rising to a hard contradiction.
